steps.text: Earthquakes and modern growth have tested the city’s buildings and setting. Preserving the historic centre requires decisions about both structural care and everyday urban needs.

takeaway: Quito’s setting explains the terrain; its successive communities explain the architecture.

name: Cuenca
title: A formal grid met an Andean valley.
deck: Cuenca brings a carefully ordered street plan into a mountain-framed setting.
question: Which factor best explains Cuenca’s setting and development?
options: A planned colonial grid within an Andean valley
A floating settlement in open ocean
A city without surrounding mountains

steps.label: THE LANDSCAPE
steps.title: Begin with the setting.
steps.text: An inland valley surrounded by the Andes offered land for settlement and regional agriculture. Rivers and changes in level formed part of the landscape around the planned core.

steps.label: THE HUMAN CHOICE
steps.title: A place becomes a city.
steps.text: Founded as a colonial town in 1557, Cuenca followed formal Spanish planning guidelines. The grid organised an administrative and agricultural centre that continued growing over centuries.

steps.label: THE TRADE-OFF
steps.title: The inheritance needs care.
steps.text: The enduring layout is only one layer of the city. Modern buildings and uses must work with inherited streets and the relationship between town and valley.

takeaway: A grid can be regular even when the wider landscape is anything but.

name: Sucre
title: Institutions helped anchor a highland city.
deck: Sucre’s role as a capital was built through administration and architecture.
question: Which factor best explains Sucre’s setting and development?
options: An Atlantic island trading post
A highland centre strengthened by civic and religious institutions
A settlement designed for Antarctic research

steps.label: THE LANDSCAPE
steps.title: Begin with the setting.
steps.text: A highland setting made Sucre an inland centre rather than a seaport. Its position must be understood alongside the regional routes connecting settlements and economic activity.

steps.label: THE HUMAN CHOICE
steps.title: A place becomes a city.
steps.text: Spanish founders established the city in the sixteenth century. Religious and civic institutions helped sustain an important centre whose architecture combined local traditions and European forms.

steps.label: THE TRADE-OFF
steps.title: The inheritance needs care.
steps.text: A change in political importance does not erase an urban inheritance. Caring for the historic city means accommodating present-day needs within its established streets and buildings.

takeaway: Institutions can make a regional setting into a lasting urban centre.

name: Potosí
title: Silver drew a city to a mountain.
deck: Potosí’s location is inseparable from ore, water infrastructure, and human labour.
question: Which factor best explains Potosí’s setting and development?
options: A natural deepwater harbour
A capital chosen only for its beach climate
Silver ore at Cerro Rico and supporting industrial systems

steps.label: THE LANDSCAPE
steps.title: Begin with the setting.
steps.text: Cerro Rico contained the silver ore that made the site economically important. The high-altitude location required supporting systems rather than offering an effortless place to build a city.

steps.label: THE HUMAN CHOICE
steps.title: A place becomes a city.
steps.text: Mining and hydraulic mills drove a vast colonial industrial complex. Aqueducts, artificial lakes, a mint, homes, and workers’ districts became parts of the same system, sustained in part by coerced labour.

steps.label: THE TRADE-OFF
steps.title: The inheritance needs care.
steps.text: The legacy includes environmental damage and continuing risks around mining. Monumental wealth and human exploitation belong in the same account of the city.

takeaway: A resource can explain a city’s location without justifying the costs of extracting it.

name: Salvador
title: A city connected a bay with higher ground.
deck: Salvador’s upper and lower districts reveal different roles within a colonial port.
question: Which factor best explains Salvador’s setting and development?
options: A bay-front port with upper and lower urban levels
A city in a landlocked desert basin
A settlement on permanent sea ice

steps.label: THE LANDSCAPE
steps.title: Begin with the setting.
steps.text: A coastal escarpment separates higher ground from a waterfront on the Bay of All Saints. Maritime access and elevation offered different advantages within one settlement.

steps.label: THE HUMAN CHOICE
steps.title: A place becomes a city.
steps.text: As Brazil’s first colonial capital, Salvador developed administrative, religious, and port functions. African, Indigenous, and European communities shaped its culture, while slavery underpinned much colonial economic activity.

steps.label: THE TRADE-OFF
steps.title: The inheritance needs care.
steps.text: Moving between levels remains part of the city’s geography. Its heritage also requires remembering the people and unequal systems behind its celebrated buildings.

takeaway: Salvador’s dramatic setting carries a complex human history, not only a colourful skyline.

name: Brasília
title: The decision came before the city.
deck: Brasília makes political planning unusually visible in the urban landscape.
question: Which factor best explains Brasília’s setting and development?
options: A medieval city that grew around an ocean harbour
A deliberately planned capital on an inland plateau
A town built inside a moving glacier

steps.label: THE LANDSCAPE
steps.title: Begin with the setting.
steps.text: An inland plateau supplied the setting for a new national capital. This was a deliberate relocation project rather than the gradual growth of a historic seaport.

steps.label: THE HUMAN CHOICE
steps.title: A place becomes a city.
steps.text: Lúcio Costa’s plan and Oscar Niemeyer’s major buildings coordinated administrative spaces, residential districts, and circulation. The capital opened in 1960 as an ambitious modern urban project.

steps.label: THE TRADE-OFF
steps.title: The inheritance needs care.
steps.text: Large-scale organisation creates distances as well as order. The lived city must meet everyday movement and social needs beyond the clarity of its famous plan.

takeaway: Sometimes the answer to why here begins with a national decision.

name: Ouro Preto
title: Gold brought building to difficult terrain.
deck: Ouro Preto’s steep streets record a mining boom and its aftermath.
question: Which factor best explains Ouro Preto’s setting and development?
options: A seaport beside the Arctic Ocean
A town planned on perfectly flat reclaimed seabed
Gold deposits in hilly terrain

steps.label: THE LANDSCAPE
steps.title: Begin with the setting.
steps.text: Hilly ground in Minas Gerais shaped the town’s routes and views. Gold deposits provided a reason to settle despite the demanding terrain.

steps.label: THE HUMAN CHOICE
steps.title: A place becomes a city.
steps.text: A late-seventeenth-century mining settlement became a major centre during the eighteenth-century gold rush. Wealth supported churches, bridges, fountains, and artistic work, alongside an economy dependent on enslaved labour.

steps.label: THE TRADE-OFF
steps.title: The inheritance needs care.
steps.text: Mining prosperity declined, but the town remained. Conservation now has to sustain daily life in a steep urban fabric built for a very different economic moment.

takeaway: A temporary resource boom can leave a permanent townscape.

name: Valparaíso
title: A port climbed its natural amphitheatre.
deck: Valparaíso’s hillside streets tell a different story from the flatter waterfront below.
question: Which factor best explains Valparaíso’s setting and development?
options: A narrow port plain backed by steep hills
An inland city surrounded by desert flats
A city built entirely on floating islands

steps.label: THE LANDSCAPE
steps.title: Begin with the setting.
steps.text: A narrow coastal plain meets steep surrounding hills. This creates a natural amphitheatre where building cannot simply extend inland on the same level.

steps.label: THE HUMAN CHOICE
steps.title: A place becomes a city.
steps.text: Port growth linked the city with international shipping. Residents adapted the hills with irregular streets, stairs, and mechanical elevators, contrasting with the more geometric layout on the plain.

steps.label: THE TRADE-OFF
steps.title: The inheritance needs care.
steps.text: The setting makes connections between levels essential. Looking after historic infrastructure and hillside neighbourhoods is part of preserving how the city actually works.

takeaway: Valparaíso’s transport systems are part of its landscape story.

name: Havana
title: A harbour anchored an Atlantic city.
deck: Old Havana records maritime activity within a larger modern capital.
question: Which factor best explains Havana’s setting and development?
options: A settlement at the source of the Ganges
A sheltered harbour with shipbuilding and defensive functions
A city with no access to the sea

steps.label: THE LANDSCAPE
steps.title: Begin with the setting.
steps.text: Havana Bay provided a sheltered maritime setting. Its relationship with the coast and harbour entrance helped organise port activity and the placement of defensive works.

steps.label: THE HUMAN CHOICE
steps.title: A place becomes a city.
steps.text: The Spanish colonial city developed into an important shipbuilding centre. Squares, houses, public buildings, and fortifications accumulated around a port connected with wider Atlantic networks.

steps.label: THE TRADE-OFF
steps.title: The inheritance needs care.
steps.text: The old centre is not an empty historic display. Maintaining homes and public spaces is as important as conserving celebrated monuments within the expanding metropolis.

takeaway: A harbour can anchor a city while generations build very different lives around it.
